Colors as objects

Source: R/manim_color.R
ManimColor.Rd

ManimColor() is upstream's color class. Colors in manimR are hex strings, so a ManimColor is a hex string that also carries its exact RGBA value; it works wherever a color is accepted, and it has upstream's methods through $: to_integer(), to_rgb(), to_int_rgb(), to_rgba(), to_int_rgba(), to_rgba_with_alpha(alpha), to_int_rgba_with_alpha(alpha), to_hex(with_alpha = FALSE), to_hsv(), to_hsl(), invert(with_alpha = FALSE), interpolate(other, alpha), darker(blend = 0.2), lighter(blend = 0.2), contrasting(threshold = 0.5, light = NULL, dark = NULL), opacity(opacity) and into(class_type). Arithmetic (+, -, *, /, %/%, %%, ^) works channel by channel with numbers or other colors, == compares values, ! inverts, & and | combine the integer values, and as.integer() gives to_integer().

Usage

ManimColor(value = NULL, alpha = 1)

RGBA(value = NULL, alpha = 1)

HSV(hsv, alpha = 1)

ManimColorDType

ManimColorClass

HSVClass

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
x$name

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
x$name <- value

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
Ops(e1, e2)

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
as.integer(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
as.character(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'ManimColor'
format(x, ...)

Arguments

value

A color name, a hex string (with # or 0x), an integer such as 0xFF0000, 3 or 4 numbers (0 to 1, or 0 to 255 when integers or above 1), or another ManimColor. For $<-, the new value of an HSV property.

alpha

Opacity, used when value has none.

hsv

Hue, saturation and value, with an optional fourth alpha.

x

A ManimColor.

name

Method or property name.

e1, e2

Operands.

...

Ignored.

Value

ManimColor(), RGBA() and HSV() return a color object: a hex string of class ManimColor (and HSV for HSV()). Its methods return colors, numeric vectors or character strings, as described above. ManimColorClass and HSVClass are the R6 class generators behind the class methods.

Details

A mobject stores its colors as plain hex strings, so wrap one to use the methods: ManimColor(sq$get_color())$darker().

ManimColorClass holds upstream's class methods: from_rgb(rgb, alpha), from_rgba(rgba), from_hex(hex_str, alpha), from_hsv(hsv, alpha), from_hsl(hsl, alpha), parse(color, alpha) (a list of colors for a vector or list) and gradient(colors, length) (upstream leaves it unimplemented; here it is color_gradient() as colors). RGBA() is another name for ManimColor(), as upstream.

HSV() is a color held as hue, saturation and value (0 to 1); $hue, $saturation and $value (or $h, $s, $v) read and set them, and arithmetic works on those channels. HSVClass has the same class methods. Upstream drops an HSV color's alpha when converting it; here it is kept.

ManimColorDType names the storage type of color values ("double").

Examples

c1 <- ManimColor("#FF0000")
c1$darker()
#> ManimColor('#CC0000')
c1$interpolate(ManimColor(BLUE), 0.5)$to_hex()
#> [1] "#AB626E"
ManimColorClass$from_hsv(c(0.5, 1, 1))
#> ManimColor('#00FFFF')
Square(color = ManimColor(0x00FF00))$get_color()
#> [1] "#00FF00"
h <- HSV(c(0.25, 1, 1))
h$hue <- 0.5
as.character(h)
#> [1] "#00FFFF"
